ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABD$, C is a point on $AD$, and $AD = 4CD$, $\angle CBD = \angle A$. A line is drawn through point D such that $DH \parallel AB$, intersecting the extension of $BC$ at point H. We have $\triangle HCD \sim \triangle HDB$. If $BC = 6$, find the length of $DH$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD=4CD$,\\
it follows that $\frac{CD}{AC}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
Given $DH\parallel AB$,\\
it leads to $\triangle HCD\sim \triangle BCA$,\\
which implies $\frac{HC}{BC}=\frac{CD}{AC}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
Since $BC=6$,\\
we find that $HC=2$ and $HB=HC+BC=8$,\\
Because $\triangle HCD\sim \triangle HDB$,\\
it can be deduced that $\frac{HC}{HD}=\frac{HD}{HB}$, thus $HD^2=HC\cdot HB=2\times 8=16$,\\
Therefore, $HD=\boxed{4}$ (the negative value has been discarded).
